messages:
jen_customer: Hey team — started seeing a bunch of 429s around 12:02 UTC, previously steady traffic. No code deploys on our side. All requests are identical and returning Retry-After: 3. Are we hitting burst credits or a quota?

alex_support: Sorry you're hitting this, jen — can you paste a sample request id or headers you got? 429 + Retry-After sounds like short-term throttle. cc @mike_sre for infra context.

jen_customer: here's a sample curl we used and the response headers:
```
curl -i -H 'Authorization: Bearer xxxxx' -d '{"input":"hello"}' https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
X-RateLimit-Limit: 100
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
Retry-After: 3
x-request-id: rwd-req-0a1b2c3d
```
No spikes in our app metrics, we get sudden short bursts from our job runner but average QPS ~5.

priya_support: Thanks. That X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0 indicates you exhausted a short window quota. Two quick things: do you have client-side retry/backoff? And are you using batch calls?

jen_customer: we do basic retry with fixed 1s delay x3. Batching only for embeddings. This is generation endpoint.

mike_sre: Quick infra note — hosted API uses a token-bucket-style burst credits system for short spikes. Customers get a steady-state rate (quota) + a small burst reserve that refills over time. Looks like your background job emitted several small bursts that consumed the burst credits. The Retry-After header is server-side; it indicates when to retry.

alex_support: Two paths: (1) short term: increase client-side smoothing so you don't send many small concurrent requests (we recommend a leaky bucket client with max_concurrency=4 and jittered exponential backoff). (2) If you need sustained higher QPS, we can look at raising your quota or discussing Dedicated capacity.

jen_customer: any recommended client config? our job runner spawns 20 workers.

mike_sre: If your workers all try at once, they blow the bucket. Suggested heuristics: limit concurrency per process, add a shared rate limiter or centralized token bucket. Example pseudocode (node/python):
```
// leaky bucket: allow N tokens per second with burst up to B
allow_rate = 5  // tokens/s
burst_capacity = 20
if tokens_available > 0: proceed
else: sleep(random(100, 500) ms) and retry with backoff
```
Also smoothing_window_ms = 1000 and refill_rate = allow_rate should be fine for interactive traffic.

priya_support: We also have a smoothing feature on the platform (server-side) called burst_smoothing that can be tuned per account for hosted customers. For short spikes we can increase your burst window from default 30s to 90s temporarily — that gives more leeway for short-lived fanout. If you want we can apply a temporary bump while you implement client-side throttling.

jen_customer: Would that affect our billing or cause any surprises?

linda_platform: Temporary smoothing bumps don't change per-token billing; they only relax the short-term throttle threshold. For long-running higher throughput you'd be charged by tokens as usual, and we'd recommend Reserved/Dedicated if you need SLA-backed throughput.

jen_customer: Ok let's do a temporary bump and we'll roll out a client-side leaky bucket. Can you set it for 24h? Also can you tell us how to detect burst-credit exhaustion programmatically?

alex_support: Done — I filed a config change: ticket#SUP-98721 to enable burst_smoothing:window=90s for your account, expires in 24h. You should see reduced 429s within ~1m. We will confirm in this thread when applied.

rate-limiter-bot: [config-change] Applied burst_smoothing(window=90s) to acct: ac_01Fxxx — effective at 2026-03-15T12:15:25Z. Expires: 2026-03-16T12:15:25Z.

mike_sre: For programmatic detection: check X-RateLimit-Remaining and X-RateLimit-Reset (or Retry-After on 429). We also emit x-burst-credits header when a burst is consumed, example: X-Burst-Credits-Left: 2. If you get Remaining==0 + Burst-Credits-Left==0, that's a clear sign. I'll ask infra to add that header consistently for easier debugging.

jen_customer: Saw the bot message, thanks. We'll implement leaky bucket and reduce workers to 6 for now. Any recommended backoff strategy?

priya_support: Start with randomized exponential backoff: initial=200ms, factor=2, max=3000ms, jitter= +-20%. Also honor Retry-After if present — treat it as authoritative. For synchronous user-facing requests you can also queue and return a polite rate-limit page instead of retrying.

alex_support: Follow-up: after smoothing bump, watch for any anomalies in latency — if credits are being consumed long-term we'll reach out. If you want a longer window or permanent change, we'll need product signoff.

jen_customer: Appreciate the quick turnaround. One last question: are burst credits shared across API keys in the same org? Our infra uses multiple keys per service.

mike_sre: Good question. Burst credits are per-account (per org) by default, not per-api-key. If you have multiple keys they draw from the same pool; that can cause surprises if different services fan out concurrently. You can request per-key isolation for enterprise accounts, but it's not the default.

jen_customer: That explains it — we have a second job that spikes at similar times. We'll coordinate and tag keys. Thanks everyone, closing for now.

alex_support: Closing notes: spike came from concurrent job workers; applied 90s smoothing for 24h; recommended client-side leaky bucket + backoff; monitoring advice: alert on x-rate-limit-remaining <= 5 or 429 spikes > 3/min. Reopen if 429s continue. :thumbsup:
